newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares seen vulnerable to further selloffs.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares seen vulnerable to further selloffs.

text.p: Belgian shares ended a rocky pre-holiday session 0.78 percent higher on Thursday, correcting a two percent fall Wednesday.

The Bel-20 index .BFX ended 18.77 points higher at 2417.87, but its one percent trading range masked much larger swings in selected shares, which moved between plus and minus three percent. Dealers blamed some short-covering in an illiquid holiday-thin market.
Analysts continue to advise caution for next week as the market is seen vulnerable to further selloffs. On Friday, the market is closed for the Assumption holiday.
Dealers said the impact of the expiry of futures and options on the Bel-20 index had been limited. "A lot of covering had been done on Thursday," one said.

Insurer Fortis AG ended 80 francs lower at 7,380 francs after swinging between 7,500 and 7,320 francs in big volume of nearly 60,000 shares. One dealer said he suspected short-covering activity in the share.

Next week, the Bel-20 index is expected to flirt with the 2,400 support level, which was tested for the third time today. A second support level is seen around 2,350. The index is now more than 200 points below the 2625 point high set on July 28.
